images.name: cover
images.title: How to write a *job description* for an AI Employee
images.sub: The eight parts it needs, how to word each duty so it can be followed, and a sample you can copy.

images.name: posting-vs-description
images.title: A posting vs. an *AI Employee job description*
head: Job posting for a person
AI Employee job description
rows: Get the right person to apply
When an email arrives, sort it into six types
Each login and what it may do there
Alone, reports or asks, for every duty
Written as exceptions, or handed to a person
images.source: Culture, perks and soft skills mostly drop out

images.name: eight-parts
images.title: The *eight parts*
head: Part
What it says
Example
rows: The job name and one person it reports to
AI Intake Coordinator, reports to the office manager
What the job exists to get done
Trigger, action and system for each task
When a web form arrives, reply and ask the intake questions
Every login and what it may do
Clio: read matters, create contacts, no billing
Alone, reports or asks, per duty
Books consults alone, asks before any refund
Urgent matters to the lawyer on duty by text
Never gives legal advice or quotes fees
Reply time, handoffs, items left open
images.source: Duties and exceptions take most of the page

images.name: sample
images.title: Sample: *AI Client Coordinator* at an accounting firm
rows: Creates the client in TaxDome and sends the engagement letter
Chases W-2s, 1099s and last year's return on a fixed schedule, email then text
Answers "where's my return?" from the status in TaxDome
Books them into the accountant's calendar
Flags a new rental property or missing income to the accountant
Hands the question to a person with the client's file

images.name: quote
images.text: If you can't write a duty as *a trigger, an action and a system,* you've found the part of the job that still needs a person.

images.name: rewrite
images.title: Rewrite the posting you *already have*
steps: Remove perks, culture and soft skills. Keep the duties list.
Sit with the person doing it
For each duty: what starts it, what they do, which system, what goes wrong.
Turn every duty into a sentence that can be followed as written.
Mark each duty alone, reports or asks, and list what it never does.
Choose the few numbers the manager will review each week.
